name: Cape Floral Region Protected Areas
blurb: Proteas, sugarbirds and seed-carrying ants in fire-driven fynbos.

tip.title: Take away fire
tip.text: Fynbos depends on fire to renew. Set Fire to -100% and watch the shrubs, then the nectar birds and seed-carrying ants that rely on them.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Cape Floral Region Protected Areas

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Table Mountain National Park, Cape Floristic Region, Fynbos). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. nodes.desc: A grass of fynbos edges and renosterveld that grazers such as the Cape mountain zebra and bontebok eat.
The top predator of the Cape mountains, where it hunts baboons and hyraxes.
Long, dry summers and mild winters drive growth in this Mediterranean-type climate.
Fynbos is a fire-prone shrubland. Fire clears old growth and releases seeds, and many plants depend on it to renew.
Break down dead plants, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

story: The Cape Floral Region at the southern tip of South Africa is the smallest of the world's six floral kingdoms. It holds over 9,000 vascular plant species, 69 percent of them endemic. Table Mountain National Park, proclaimed in 1998, is part of the World Heritage Site.
matters: Much of this diversity belongs to fynbos, a fire-prone, Mediterranean-type shrubland. Fynbos still faces severe human-caused threats.
